subject: HealthGrid: deployment gating & compliance evidence — recap & asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: HealthGrid: deployment gating & compliance evidence — recap & asks

Riley — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed asks so nothing falls through the cracks.

Call summary (30 min):
- Primary driver: HealthGrid will process PHI in several flows (appointment reminders + clinician notes ingestion).
- Security gating: BAA required; SOC2 Type II evidence; encryption-at-rest details; audit/log access for security and compliance teams.
- Performance: target <150ms p50 for patient-facing inferencing; some batch workloads ok at higher latency.

Redwood deployment tradeoffs we discussed:
- Hosted API (fastest): fastest onboarding, we can sign a BAA and provide SOC2 artifacts. Good if isolation requirements are moderate and HealthGrid accepts shared tenancy controls.
- Dedicated capacity: dedicated GPU pools + VPC peering available. Stronger isolation and predictable throughput (recommended if you need SLA-backed latency and consistent concurrency).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full private control plane and optional on-prem package for environments that require air-gapped or regulated data center controls. Longer lead time and procurement.

Asks / next steps for HealthGrid (please confirm):
1) Can you confirm which data flows will carry PHI vs non-PHI? (e.g., clinician notes ingestion = PHI)
2) Do you require on-prem air-gapped hosting, or would Dedicated with VPC peering + BAA be acceptable?
3) Procurement: timeline for PO and who will lead (procurement@healthgrid.io contact)?
4) Security evidence: timeline to review SOC2 Type II and BAA draft (we can share redacted report).

Attachments: Redwood-HIPAA-sprint-checklist.pdf (summary of typical evidence we provide).

I'll follow up with a short list of technical questions for Karthik to confirm sizing. Thanks — Jordan

--

Jordan — thanks, that matches our notes. Quick answers and clarifications:

- PHI scope: clinician notes ingestion (batch and near-real-time) and appointment reminders (low-sensitivity metadata). Both will be in scope for at least the pilot.
- Preference: we would prefer Dedicated capacity with VPC peering if it meets encryption and logging requirements. On-prem is an option but will add procurement constraints and is not our first choice.
- Procurement: Emily from procurement (procurement@healthgrid.io) will own PO timing — target to have budget sign-off by mid-September.
- Security asks: Asha (cc'd) will share a short spreadsheet of evidence items; SOC2 Type II and a BAA are must-haves. We also need confirmation of key management (customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed KMS with HSM?) and encryption key rotation practices.

I've attached the security intake sheet we typically use: HealthGrid-internal-security-questions.xlsx. Asha, please flag anything else for Jordan/Redwood.

—Riley

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: HealthGrid: deployment gating & compliance evidence — recap & asks

Hi all — a few technical clarifications so we size the Dedicated pilot correctly and confirm feasibility for customer-managed KMS:

1) Traffic profile: Riley — can you provide expected peak QPS and average tokens per request (or average prompt + response length)? That will determine GPU sizing and autoscale thresholds.
2) Retention: what are your retention windows for request/response logs and cached KV? Redwood can configure per-route retention; defaults are 90 days. If you need longer (365 days) we can enable with enterprise plan.
3) KMS: Dedicated supports VPC peering and two KMS options — Redwood-managed encryption (with HSM-backed keys) or customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS (we can do envelope encryption). If you require on-prem HSM, that pushes us toward Private with a longer lead time.
4) Audit access: we can provide time-bound access for your security team to pull audit logs; confirm the list of principals and acceptable timeframe.

Quick note on latency: for patient-facing inference (p50 <150ms) we recommend reserving an instance pool sized for peak concurrency (we'll propose config after QPS). For the pilot we can commit a 2-week SLA-backed window to validate latency before a longer-term SLA.

I'll draft a short sizing questionnaire we can pass to Riley to capture QPS and payload sizes.

—Karthik
